issues.legal_issue: Open land leased for construction of buildings intended for covered uses is let for those uses and is subject to the rent-control regime.
material_facts: The suits sought recovery of rent relating to land that was not being used for agricultural purposes.
The land was in an area covered by the Act.
Each lease was taken with a view to constructing buildings for residential, business, industrial or office purposes.
The suits were brought in an ordinary civil court, and the defendants contested that court’s jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The leases were for covered uses, so Part II of the Act applied to the premises and the ordinary civil court lacked jurisdiction; the special courts specified by the Act had jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(8) includes non-agricultural land within the meaning of premises, and section 6(1) applies Part II to premises let for residence, education, business, trade or storage in specified areas. A letting for one of those purposes includes letting land to achieve that purpose by constructing buildings, as well as achieving it without construction. Under section 28, the special courts have jurisdiction over the relevant suits. The Court approved Vinayak Gopal v. Laxman Kashinath, I.L.R. (1956) Bom. 827. It did not decide whether section 15 would prevent the lessee from letting out buildings constructed on the land.

rule.if: ordinary_civil_rent_arrears_suit and non_agricultural_land and within_covered_area and leased_for_covered_use_by_construction

predicates.ordinary_civil_rent_arrears_suit: A party brought an ordinary civil-court suit seeking recovery of rent arrears concerning the leased premises.
predicates.non_agricultural_land: The leased premises consisted of land that was not being used for agricultural purposes.
predicates.within_covered_area: The leased premises were situated in an area covered by the rent-control regime.
predicates.leased_for_covered_use_by_construction: The land was leased so that buildings could be constructed on it for residence, education, business, trade or storage.

issues.definition: When an ordinary civil-court rent-arrears suit concerns non-agricultural land in a covered area leased for a covered use to be achieved by construction, the special rent court has exclusive jurisdiction.
